_note: Hand labels for the comps model comparison (Phase 6 step 5), written 2026-10-17 from business comparability: products, customers and economics. true = a reasonable peer for multiples. Candidates are those found for the valuation date 2026-10-11 (Damodaran industry, size band).

AAPL._reasons: Hardware makers kept (PCs, servers, consumer peripherals); printing, enterprise storage, banking machines, haptics licensing and photography dropped

BA._reasons: All aerospace or defense: GE is GE Aerospace since 2024; HII is a defense prime; Howmet and TransDigm are aerospace component makers

CAT._reasons: Heavy machinery and engines kept (Terex and Oshkosh compete directly); cement and aggregates are customers, not peers

DE._reasons: Farm and outdoor machinery kept; grain traders and ingredient processors dropped (Damodaran's Farming/Agriculture mixes them)

KO._reasons: Branded beverage companies kept; Zevia and Reed's are too small and loss-making to give a meaningful multiple

MCD._reasons: Restaurant operators and franchisors kept; contract food service and delivery platforms dropped

MSFT._reasons: Large software companies kept; Roper is a diversified industrial-software holding

NKE._reasons: Footwear brands kept; Smartbird (former Allbirds) is now a computer-services shell

NVDA._reasons: All semiconductor companies; differences in end markets show in the multiples, not in peer status

SNOW._reasons: Cloud and data software kept (MongoDB is the closest); domains and small-business website builders, and low-margin managed hosting, dropped
